title: Utah's 2nd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Utah's 2nd Congressional District election takes place under a court-ordered redistricting map that redrew boundaries across all four of Utah's congressional districts. The new district encompasses Davis, Weber, Box Elder, Cache, and Rich counties in northern Utah, including Hill Air Force Base. The Republican primary between incumbent U.S. Representative Blake Moore (previously of the 1st District) and state Representative Karianne Lisonbee has been highly competitive, with Lisonbee criticizing Moore's past support for anti-gerrymandering reforms and Moore emphasizing his leadership role as House Republican Conference Vice Chair. The Democratic nominee is Peter Crosby, who advanced without a primary contest, and third-party candidates include Libertarian Daniel Cottam, Independent American Carlton Bowen, and unaffiliated candidate Robert Moesinger.
polling_note: No general election polling was found for this race as of mid-June 2026. The Republican primary is scheduled for June 23, 2026, and the general election will follow on November 3, 2026.

candidates.name: Blake Moore
candidates.summary: Blake Moore is a U.S. Representative who has represented Utah's 1st Congressional District since 2021 and is now running in the newly redrawn 2nd District due to court-ordered redistricting. He serves as Vice Chair of the House Republican Conference—the first Utahn ever elected to House or Senate leadership—and sits on the House Ways and Means and Budget Committees. Moore emphasizes his leadership role and track record of passing legislation, including bills related to tax policy, public lands, and military modernization.

candidates.name: Karianne Lisonbee
candidates.summary: Karianne Lisonbee is a Utah State Representative and former House Majority Whip who is challenging Blake Moore in the Republican primary for Utah's 2nd Congressional District. She has served in the Utah House of Representatives for nearly a decade, including as chair of the House Judiciary Committee, and previously served on the Syracuse City Council. Lisonbee campaigns on reducing federal spending and the national debt, describing herself as a proven conservative with an A+ NRA rating and a 100% pro-life voting record.

candidates.name: Peter Crosby
candidates.summary: Peter Crosby is the Democratic nominee for Utah's 2nd Congressional District, having advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot as the uncontested candidate. He has a background in analytics and operations for a Fortune 500 company before working at Utah State University in institutional research and teaching as an adjunct instructor in the Center for Anticipatory Intelligence. Crosby currently works as a director and consultant for a research company supporting higher education, and he campaigns on integrity, practical solutions, and fighting for affordable housing and honest government.

forecast.rationale: No general election polling is available (based_on_poll_count=0), so this assessment relies entirely on structural and contextual indicators. The newly drawn northern Utah district encompasses Davis, Weber, Box Elder, Cache, and Rich counties — a heavily Republican region in a state where the GOP holds all four U.S. House seats and the presidential margin was approximately +20 points in 2024. The Republican primary (June 23) between incumbent Blake Moore and state Rep. Karianne Lisonbee is described as highly competitive, but the general election winner regardless of the primary outcome is overwhelmingly expected to be Republican. The Democratic nominee, Peter Crosby, advanced without a primary and has limited statewide profile. Third-party and unaffiliated candidates (Libertarian Daniel Cottam, Independent American Carlton Bowen, Robert Moesinger) are further marginal. Key uncertainties: (1) the Republican primary is unresolved as of this writing; (2) the court-ordered map is new, so exact partisan composition is not validated by prior election results in this precise configuration; and (3) zero polling exists. The safe_r rating (≈95%+ Republican win probability) reflects Utah's strong Republican lean and the weakness of the Democratic and minor-party field, while low confidence acknowledges the absence of polling and the untested district lines.
